sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 19-08-2017.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 19-08-2017 at about 8.00 to 8.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in a two wheeler bearing Reg.No. KA-04-HU-9823 from Boralinganapalya side towards Kunigal side, which was ridden by one Lokesh and after crossing of NH-48 by putting Krishnappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176869061/
1 indicator, near Neralamma temple at Boralinganapalya, at that time, the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing No. KA.18-F-823 driven the same at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to CHC, Kunigal wherein first aid treatment was given and for further treatment he was shifted to A.C. Giri hospital,
wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and took treatment for the accidental injuries and discharged with an advice of regular followup treatment and bed rest.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 55 years and was doing agricultural work and thereby earning Rs.2,00,000/- p.a. and also doing centering and bar bending working and earning Rs.1,000/- per day.
Due to the accidental injuries, petitioner is not able to do his work and lost his income.
The respondent is the owner and internal insurer of the bus is liable to pay compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- with interest.

3. After service of notice respondent- owner of the KSRTC bus appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by contending that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant and fanciful.

It has denied the cause and manner of accident, age, occupation,
income of the petitioner and also the treatment taken by the petitioner for the injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident.

Further contended that, the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing No.
KA-18-F-823 was proceeding from Chikkamangalur to Bengaluru on the left side of the road , while proceeding so on NH-48 which is four paths road having a road median separating two paths each side, at that time the rider of the scooter who came from the cross road in a rash and negligent manner along with pillion rider without wearing helmet and that too without observing the vehicular movements on the highway and dashed against this respondent's vehicle.
Accordingly, the respondent prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-18-F-823 and as a result he sustained injuries ?
2. Whether the petitioner proves the age and earnings of the petitioners as stated in the claim petition?
3. Whether the petitioner is enti- tled for compensation?
If so, how much?

4. What Order or Award?

sentences.text: In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1, through him got marked Ex.P1 to 12.
Also examined MRO of A.C. Giri hospital as PW.2, through him got marked the documents at Ex.P13 to Ex.P16.

On the other hand, the respondent examined the driver of the bus as RW.1.
6.
Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;

 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, spot sketch, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 7.
9.

On perusal of Ex.P1, FIR which is registered on the basis of the first information given by one B.S.
Anandaswamy who is an eyewitness by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-18-F-823.

The contents of Ex.P2 complaint and Ex.P1 FIR supports the contention of the petitioner about the rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-18-F-823 which is owned and insured by the respondent.
In continuation of Ex.P1 & 2, the police drawn spot mahazar and spot sketch which are marked as Ex.P3 & P.4.

On perusal of Ex.P3 &
P.4 spot mahazar and sketch the accident spot is within 5 feet from the edge of the road.

10. The Ex.P5 is the IMV report wherein the motor cycle bearing No. KA.04-HU-9823 has got damaged in its front number late, front both side radiators, left side handle folded, pressed, front both side mirror, left side fuel tank pressed inwards, left side crash guard pressed, left side head light, left side front footrest, left side rear Larry guard pressed, front head light shield etc. and the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-18-F-823 has got damages in its front left side bumper, front left side shape pressed inward, front left side headlight and radiator pressed and damaged, left side body pressed and front interior shape.
This shows that the front left side of the Bus bearing No.KA-18-F-823 dashed against the motorcycle in which the petitioner was proceeding.
Thus it can be construed that the offending bus dashed against the motor cycle and it shows that the bus dashed against the motorcycle as the driver of the bus was negligent.
Thereby the contents of Ex.P.5 falsifies the defence of the respondent about the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.

sentences.text: The respondent in the written statement and also in the evidence of RW.1 admitted the accident but denied the negligence and manner of the accident as stated by the petitioner.
Except the evidence of RW.1 no other documents or evidence is lead by the respondent in support of their defence.

12. The charge sheet as per Ex.P7 is filed against the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-18-F-823 for the offence punishable under Sec.279, 337, 304(A), 338 of IPC wherein the IO opined that rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus is the sole reason for the accident.
No grounds are made out to disbelieve the contents of charge sheet.

The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus:
In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to supra and appreciated the same in the proper perspective and recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in the affirmative.

sentences.text: But it has recorded the finding in the negative on the above issues by adverting to certain statements of evidence of AW- 1 and referring to certain alleged discrepancies in the FIR without appreciating entire evidence of AW- 1 and AW-2 on record properly and also not assigned valid reasons in not accepting their testimony.

The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304-A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.

The registration of FIR and filing of the charge-sheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants.

Hence, by relying on the said precedent and denial in respect of police documents marked at Ex.P1 to 7, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-18-F-823.
13.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: 15. As per well settled principle of law the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
In the absence of rebuttal evidence there are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner.

All the materials available on record leading to show that,
petitioner sustained injuries in the accident took place on 19-08-2017 which is caused by the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-18-F-823 which belongs to the respondent.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
The Ex.P6 wound certificate petitioner has got grievous as well as simple injuries in the said accident.
16. The respondent examined its driver but has not made any grounds to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence adduced by the petitioner.
The charge sheet is not challenged by the respondent.
Thus, it shows that the respondent herein has no grounds for defence and has not disputed the allegations of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
17.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the vehicle of the respondent.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 55 years.
As per the Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P11 shows that the year of birth of the petitioner as 1968.
The accident was occurred in the year 2017.
Hence, as per this document the petitioner was aged about 49 years.
In the medical records the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 50 years.
In the petition itself he has averred that he was admitted to A.C. Giri hospital as per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P8.
As per Ex.P8 the petitioner has took treatment as an inpatient from 20-08-2017 to 07-09-2017 and has sustained dislocation of middle and distal phalanx of left thumb.
As per wound certificate there are four injuries out of which one injury is grievous injury and other three are simple injuries.
By considering the nature of the injuries and the period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.65,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.

b) Medical expenses: The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P9 and P.12 for Rs.6,273/-
and Rs.2,810/- respectively.
The said bills is not seriously disputed by the respondent and no grounds are made out to disbelieve the bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding off the same i.e., Rs.10,000/-
( C ) TOWARDS DIET, FOOD, NOURISHMENT, CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

sentences.text: As already observed the Ex.P-8, makes it amply clear that the petitioner underwent treatment for the injuries sustained by him.
The petitioner has produced wound certificate as per Ex.P6 which shows that the petitioner sustained grievous injury as well as simple injury.
During the said period the petitioner might have taken assistance from others and taken diet food.
On consideration of the injuries sustained by the petitioner this Tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and proper to award an amount of Rs.25,000/- under this head.
(D) TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNING CAPACITY ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
It is necessary to note that the loss of future earning capacity cannot be presumed and has to be proved with cogent evidence.
But interestingly the petitioner though claims that he is unable to do any work and has become disabled he has not put in any efforts to prove the disability by examining the doctor, who treated him.
In fact he has not even produced the disability certificate issued by competent authority.
In the absence of any such material piece of evidence, it is very difficult for this Court to assess the disability and thereby assess the loss of earning capacity due to disability.
This makes it clear that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability.

Further in the judgment reported in 2020(4) KCCR 2621 between Sri Nandish K. V/s United India Insurance Co. Ltd. & another wherein it is held that no compensation could be awarded towards the loss of earning capacity if physical disability do not effect claimant's capacity to work.

entities.text: Sri Nandish K. V/s United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the absence of evidence to show the disability,
this court has no option but to hold that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability which has resulted in reduction of his income and hence he is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
(E) TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner has not made out any evidence or grounds to hold that he sustained the loss of income during the laid down period.
Inspite of sufficient time the petitioner has not produced any documents to show that there is loss of total income in the laid up period.
Hence, in the absence of any evidence, petitioner is not entitled for any amount under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
F) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained simple and grievous injuries in the accident.
As per Ex.P8 the petitioner was admitted to hospital on 20.08.2017 and discharged on 07.09.2017.
Thereby the petitioner has spent 19 days in the hospital as an inpatient.

Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.1,000/-
per day i.e., Rs.19,000/- is awarded towards attendant charges.

(G) TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES AND Krishnappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176869061/
6 ENJOYMENT OF LIFE:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award him a reasonable sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
To sum up the above discussion, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following Towards pain and sufferings - Rs. 65,000/-

Towards Medical expenses - Rs. 10,000/-
Towards diet, food, - Rs. 25,000/-
nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges  Towards loss of future earning - NIL  capacity  Loss of income during laid up - NIL  period  Towards attendant charges - Rs. 19,000/-
Towards loss of amenities - Rs. 20,000/-
Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent is the owner and there is a internal insurance to the offending vehicle.
No grounds are made to consider the contributory negligence.

Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
19.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.1,39,000/- (Rupees one lakh thirty nine thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondent.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6%

Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.1,39,000/- (Rupees one lakh thirty nine thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondent.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
